note: One row per encoder version, append-only. See PROVENANCE.md. The first row records a large, known defect in the Python adapter rather than hiding it: read its note before using these numbers for anything.

rows.note: First measurement of the Python adapter against real code. The function count is NOT the project's: toml has 56 functions and this run found 14. The Python adapter only walks top-level function definitions, so every method inside a class is invisible to it, while the TypeScript adapter walks recursively and finds methods. That asymmetry is a defect in the encoder, not in this corpus, and it is why the opaque rate of 14.2% is a measurement of the 25% of the project the adapter can see. Fixing it is an encoder change and therefore a new IR version with its own row.

The first credible measurement of this corpus. The Python adapter now walks recursively, so methods inside classes and functions inside functions are found: 56 functions, matching an independent count of 'def' occurrences in the source, against 14 at IR-4. ordered.py and tz.py report statements for the first time. The opaque rate FELL slightly, from 14.2% to 13.6%, which falsifies the prediction that the hidden methods were disproportionately full of semantics the IR cannot represent; see the IR-5 entry in the experiment log.

IR-7 Receiver: a member call keeps the entity it acts on, as parsed, and ir_schema moves to 4. Statement counts, function counts, opacity and the number of collision groups are unchanged, because no statement became representable and none stopped being; the collision FINGERPRINTS changed for functions containing member calls, which was expected and not predicted stable, because new computational information is now in the fingerprint. The receiver is not used for resolution in this round.

IR-9 classifies every statement as semantic, non-semantic or metadata, and only an unrepresented SEMANTIC statement counts as opaque. The statement count changed legitimately because 8 non-semantic and 7 metadata statements left the denominator: they carry no execution semantics and were previously counted as unrepresented semantics. Intrinsic fingerprints changed wherever a function body contained a docstring or a bare string statement, which was expected and not predicted stable. Nothing else changed: no new resolution, no import modelling, no loop or exception representation.

C-2 changed the Python adapter, and this corpus contains no yield, so every measured value is identical to its IR-9 row: 345 semantic statements, 34 opaque, 8 non-semantic and 7 metadata statements left the denominator, and both collision fingerprints are unchanged. The row exists so that every encoder version has a measurement of every corpus, and its being identical is the result.

C-3 reclassified this corpus's single `with`: exception-handling 4 to 3, scoped-resource 1. Every other measured value is identical to the C-2 row, including both collision fingerprints, because the function holding that `with` is in no collision group. 345 semantic statements, 34 opaque, 8 non-semantic and 7 metadata statements left the denominator.

C-4 classifies nested defs, and this corpus has none: its single declaration is a nested class_definition at decoder.py line 644, which C-4 leaves as declaration because a constructed class is an entity question rather than a function construction. Every measured value is identical to the C-3 row, and no movement was manufactured. 345 semantic statements, 34 opaque, 8 non-semantic and 7 metadata statements left the denominator.

C-5 changed the Python adapter's bare-await handling and this corpus contains no await at all, so every measured value is identical to the C-4 row. 345 semantic statements, 34 opaque, 8 non-semantic and 7 metadata statements left the denominator.

R-1A, ir_schema 6. No await in this corpus: categories, counts and collision-group membership identical to C-5; both fingerprint values changed with the schema number, as in every corpus. 8 non-semantic and 7 metadata statements left the denominator.
